item.title: Report: Mossad chief in Washington as Netanyahu pushes for renewed Iran strikes
item.description:
Axios reports Mossad chief Roman Gofman meets senior US officials in Washington as Netanyahu presses Trump to resume strikes on Iran, despite the President's reluctance.
(Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' North American desk is keeping you updated until the start of Shabbat in New York. The time posted automatically on all Israel National News articles, however, is Israeli time.)

item.title: Shabbat Shalom from Israel!
item.description:
Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' Israel desk is stopping its round-the-clock news updates at this time in honor of Shabbat. Jerusalem candle lighting time is 16:01 on Friday. Our North American desk will keep you informed until the 16:21 EST candle lighting time in New York.
The updates from Israel will resume Saturday night, following the conclusion of Shabbat at 17:19 in Jerusalem.
Shabbat Shalom!

item.title: Eisenkot backs Elisaf Peretz: "I trust him, I am the one to criticize
item.description:
Yashar! party chairman MK Gadi Eisenkot expressed his support for MK Elisaf Peretz and his family.
"I embrace Miriam Peretz, and I trust Elisaf. I know that he trusts me and the decisions I make, and will continue to make," Eisenkot wrote.
Eisenkot said that some members of his party and their families, including bereaved families, have been receiving thousands of harsh and abusive messages.
"People are entitled to disagree and criticize, but there is no place for incitement or threats," he stressed. "If anyone has a problem with the path I am setting, I am the one they should direct their criticism toward."

item.description: One thing that won't help is blaming Bibi: Americans who trash Prime Minister Netanyahu don’t revile him because he is the prime minister but because he is the prime minister of the Jewish State. Removing him will not affect antisemitism. Opinion.

item.title: IDF: Over 93,000 tents enter Gaza ahead of winter
item.description: Over 8,600 trucks deliver winter supplies to Gaza, while COGAT and international partners coordinate medical aid and repairs to water and sewage systems.

item.title: The lost compass and the decision awaiting Matan Kahana
item.description: After bereaved mother Esti Yaniv's painful remarks, Rabbi Yaakov Yakir opposes a government backed by Arab parties, criticizes Kobi Richter's political role and urges former classmate Matan Kahana to choose Jewish unity at this decisive moment.

item.title: Demilitarization plan becomes a gift to Hamas
item.description: Minister Orit Strock sharply criticizes the Board of Peace and its head, Nickolay Mladenov, saying the new demilitarization plan meets Hamas's demands and leaves weapons in Gaza. She urges Israel to block it and insist on full demilitarization.

item.title: Police deploy rooftop snipers in Rahat: 'Gunfire will be met with gunfire'
item.description: Following shooting incidents and criminal activity in southern Israel, district police commander orders snipers deployed on rooftops in Rahat.

item.description: The pre-Islamic Near East can thus be considered, within the symbolic geography of Genesis, a meeting place of Ham and Shem.

item.title: The wells they could not bury
item.description: Why would anyone deliberately destroy a source of water in a land where every drop counts? Something remarkably similar happened in Gaza in 2005, after Israel withdrew from the territory and expelled its Jewish communities.

item.title: The Voice and the Hands: What was signed on the Mount of Olives
item.description: On 24 Cheshvan 5787, sixty people signed a scroll in Jerusalem. They now have a morning after, and the work has already begun.

item.title: A crisis of faith over politics? Enough, you've gone too far
item.description: Shlomo Kook questions how election results can cause a "crisis of faith". He says Jewish faith has survived repeated persecution and needs no stamp of approval from any political bloc.

item.title: Ahead of IDF enlistment, Ashkelon hesder yeshiva student completes Talmud
item.description: Ashkelon's hesder yeshiva honored second-year IDF recruits. Netael Yehuda Rosenberg completed the Babylonian Talmud, which he began studying in 10th grade. Rabbis blessed the recruits, emphasizing Torah study alongside military service.

item.title: Dr. Chana Katan asks: Where have the election promises gone?
item.description: In a video column on Arutz Sheva, Dr. Chana Katan criticizes shifting political positions on conscription, stressing an unchanged security need: more IDF combat soldiers and a fairer sharing of the burden.

item.title: Haredi draft evaders jailed by military to receive grants at Bnei Brak tribute event
item.description: Special event to be held in Bnei Brak on Saturday night, during which grants totaling NIS 147,000 will be distributed to yeshiva students who were held in military prison.

item.title: Ponevezh dispute: Supreme Court allows temporary stay, sets terms for vacating campus
item.description: In interim ruling, Supreme Court allows Rabbi Markovitz's followers to remain at Ponevezh until August 2027, subject to a commitment to vacate and payments totaling millions of shekels.

item.title: Military boots raised suspicions: Secret Gaza border map seized from Palestinian home
item.description: Police notice Palestinian Arab man wearing military boots, search of his home uncovers classified map of the Gaza border area, knives and an airsoft pistol.

item.title: Akunis warns Palestinian state would lead to another October 7
item.description: Speaking to American influencers in Peduel, Israel’s Consul General in New York Ofir Akunis calls Judea and Samaria Israel’s 'protective shield.'

item.title: Former Mossad official warns: Iran is edging toward the nuclear threshold
item.description: Former Mossad official Haim Tomer agrees with former Mossad chief Dadi Barnea's warning, but believes a nuclear deal with Iran is preferable to having no agreement.

item.title: Raid footage: Loaded gun found on woman, hundreds of thousands of shekels seized
item.description: During a search of the Azazmeh compound, Border Police officers found a loaded handgun concealed on a 20-year-old woman and NIS 315,000 in cash in the home.

item.title: Microsoft outage also affects Globes: Website and app updates disrupted
item.description: Microsoft outages persist this morning, affecting Outlook, Teams and Microsoft 365. Globes said its website and app are not updating due to the outage. Microsoft said repairs were not progressing as expected after detecting infrastructure overloads.

item.title: Modi'in Illit: Miriam Ben Hamo dies after rare birth complication, leaving eight children
item.description: Miriam Bracha Ben Hamo, 40, a mother of eight from Modi'in Illit, dies at Sheba Medical Center after suffering an amniotic fluid embolism during childbirth at Mayanei Hayeshua Medical Center.
